findings.note: Both halves pair the liquid measure with the solid measure at the same scale tier (small-small, large-large), so a player reading 'drop is to pinch as dose is to handful' finds a consistent corresponding-scale relation. Both halves read as: "smallest unit of liquid corresponds to smallest unit of solid" and "largest unit of liquid corresponds to largest unit of solid".

notes:
The dimensional-similarity set has a valid unintended cross-reading: liquid measures (drop/dose) and solid measures (pinch/handful) line up as parallel small→large tiers, so the set can be solved by matching same-scale-tier rather than the intended single-dimension progression.
- set-dimensional-similarity: drop:dose (liquid) and pinch:handful (solid) form parallel small/large tiers across two substance categories, letting a solver validly read 'liquid small:solid small :: liquid large:solid large' instead of the intended single-scale progression.
  Try: Replace pinch:handful with a pair on the same liquid-measure dimension as drop:dose, e.g. drop:dose :: splash:draught (or drop:dose :: trickle:flood), so both pairs progress along one shared kind of measure rather than two substance types.
  Or: Replace drop:dose with a solid/dry-measure pair matching pinch:handful's category, e.g. grain:ounce :: pinch:handful, removing the liquid/solid split entirely.
  Or: Keep both pairs but change one word so the units no longer align tier-for-tier (e.g. swap handful for a non-parallel large solid unit like sackful), breaking the corresponding-scale cross-reading.
Do not change: set-agent-instrument, set-taxonomic, set-time-activity — no allowlisted finding touches them.
